Ananuri Fortress

A 17th-century castle on the shore of the Zhinvali reservoir — the most photogenic stop on the Georgian Military Highway.

Time needed
1 h
From Tbilisi
70 km · 1:20
Road
Paved
Car needed
Economy class
Season
All year
Entry
free

Ananuri is where everyone stops on the way to Kazbegi, and deservedly so. The fortress stands on a rocky spur above the Zhinvali reservoir, its lower walls dropping straight into turquoise water, and the whole composition looks almost staged.

The site developed from the 13th century onwards, but what stands today is largely 17th century. It was the seat of the Dukes of Aragvi and a defensive knot controlling the Aragvi valley — in other words, the only road north. In 1739 the rival Duke of Ksani besieged and burned it; scorch marks are still visible on the tower walls.

Three main structures sit inside the curtain wall:

  • The Church of the Assumption (1689), with lavish stone carving on its south facade, a vine cross and two lions
  • The older, plainer Church of the Virgin, with fragments of fresco surviving inside
  • The square keep, climbable by internal stairs, with a full view over the reservoir from the top

The carving on the Assumption facade deserves a slow look; it is among the best examples of late medieval Georgian decoration anywhere. Water levels change through the year: in spring the reservoir laps close to the walls, while by late summer it drops and leaves a wide band of exposed shoreline.

Practical advice

An hour covers the site comfortably. The climb up the keep is a narrow, steep stone stair with no handrail, so take care in wet weather or with children. Dress rules apply inside the churches, and scarves are left by the door. Parking beside the road is free, and there are stalls selling churchkhela, honey and coffee, plus toilets. In winter the wind is fierce and the walls ice over, so proper boots make a difference.

How to get there from Tbilisi

Head north from Tbilisi on the Georgian Military Highway (E117) past Mtskheta and on towards Zhinvali — 70 km, about an hour and twenty minutes. The road is asphalt throughout and in good condition, though beyond Zhinvali it narrows and is cut into the cliff, so overtake with care. The fortress is directly on the right-hand side with a clear sign and a large car park. Fuel is available at Natakhtari and Zhinvali. An economy car is entirely sufficient all year round.
